question.:question/problem:
The arrows show $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. Solid grid lines are one unit apart; dotted lines divide each square in half.

![](images/89/89ead421f6a93de9dd52418fa041a4b849d131ea89a87fb18c5f118326e60c57.png)

Given that $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.

$\lambda=$ {{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Construct the known component $\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{b}$ from $O$, and call its endpoint $P$. Count signed horizontal and vertical grid displacements:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\overrightarrow{OP} &=\frac{3}{2}\,(1, -1)=\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{3}{2}\right). \\
\overrightarrow{PC} &=(2, -4).
\end{aligned}
$$

![](images/54/5447bc67b11cfc569d5a04eb6e94164ada1fa82782ba423722a3c6bd01d70e4b.png)

Compare the remaining displacement with $\mathbf{a}$, whose grid displacement is $(2, -4)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Horizontal scale} &=\frac{2}{2}=1 \\
\text{Vertical scale} &=\frac{-4}{-4}=1
\end{aligned}
$$

The scale is positive, so the remaining vector has the same direction as $\mathbf{a}$. Thus $\overrightarrow{PC}=\mathbf{a}$. By the triangle law,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c} &=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC} \\
&=\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{a} \\
&=\mathbf{a}+\frac{3}{2}\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are not parallel, so their coefficients are unique. Matching the coefficient of $\mathbf{a}$ gives $\lambda=1$.
